corrections.current: Verified: you may qualify if you have a current diagnosed condition, an in-service injury, illness, or event, and a medical link between them - and you were discharged under other than dishonorable conditions.
corrections.proposed: Verified: you may qualify if you have a current condition affecting your mind or body, you served on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive duty training, and your condition is linked to service - it started or was caused during service, an existing condition was made worse by service, or a service-connected disability appeared after you left. You must have been discharged under other than dishonorable conditions.
corrections.evidence: https://www.va.gov/disability/eligibility/ - lists both (1) a current illness or injury that affects your mind or body and (2) service on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive duty training, plus at least one of: in-service, pre-service (condition made worse by service), or post-service (disability related to active duty that didn't appear until after service). Current text omits the aggravation (pre-service) and post-service paths.

categories.notes: Summary ('Tax-free monthly compensation for conditions connected to your service') matches va.gov/disability/ ('a monthly tax-free payment to Veterans who got sick or injured while serving'). Hub page confirms accredited attorney, claims agent, or VSO representative can help file, and filing online/phone/mail/fax. BDD window 180-90 days before separation confirmed; page also requires availability for VA exams within 45 days of filing and a completed Separation Health Assessment - Part A Self Assessment form at submission (optional detail, not a correction to the existing step). Eligibility page notes OTH/bad conduct/dishonorable discharges may not qualify but points to discharge upgrade or VA Character of Discharge review. Documents list (DD-214, service medical records, current treatment records, buddy/lay statements) not contradicted; the evidence detail lives on a separate 'evidence needed' page not in sources, so not re-verified field-by-field. va.gov hub showed a banner for scheduled maintenance on Oct 1, 2026 (sign-in tools unavailable) - transient.

Health benefits hotline 877-222-VETS (8387) confirmed on va.gov/health-care/; page says you can apply online, by phone, by mail, or in person (current step omits mail/in person - acceptable, not an error). Services confirmed: primary/specialty care, prescriptions, mental health (PTSD, MST, depression, grief, anxiety), community care. 8 priority groups based on service history, disability rating, income, Medicaid eligibility, and other benefits; Priority Group 6 explicitly covers toxic-exposure categories (Camp Lejeune, TERA, radiation, Agent Orange) and post-11/11/1998 combat service, so 'toxic-exposure status (PACT Act)' as a factor is supported. PACT Act page confirms direct enrollment without first applying for disability benefits for Vietnam/Gulf War/Iraq/Afghanistan/post-9/11 combat zone/GWOT veterans and those exposed to toxins during service; no deadline, expansion effective March 5, 2024. Telehealth not explicitly confirmed on fetched excerpts (step only says 'ask about' - not a factual claim). Documents (DD-214, income info if required, insurance cards) not contradicted; not itemized on fetched pages.

Education hub confirms tuition/school costs, living allowances, VET TEC 2.0 high-tech training, Yellow Ribbon, counseling; eligible groups include veterans, active duty, Guard/Reserve, and qualified family members. Hub steps include applying, getting a Certificate of Eligibility, and using the GI Bill Comparison Tool. GI Bill Hotline 888-442-4551. Transfer page (last updated Sept 1, 2026): at least 6 years of service on the date the request is approved + agree to 4 more years; DoD decides; must request while still serving via milConnect; child can use only after sponsor completes 10 years, must be under 26 with HS diploma/equivalent - existing text accurate. Percentage tiers 50% (90-179 days) through 100% (36+ months) confirmed; exceptions: Purple Heart on/after 9/11/2001 or service-connected disability discharge after 30+ continuous days qualify for 100% (optional addition, not an error). 'Meet the School Certifying Official' step not explicitly stated on the fetched pages - unverified this quarter but consistent with standard VA enrollment process; not flagged as wrong. Documents (DD-214, COE, transcripts) not contradicted.

Hub: VA-backed loans help Veterans, service members, and survivors buy, build, improve, or refinance; 'nearly 90% of VA-backed loans are made with no down payment'; borrowers still need required credit and income. The va.gov hub page itself does not mention PMI; 'no private mortgage insurance' confirmed via WebSearch snippets from benefits.va.gov/homeloans (main pillars: no down payment, competitive rates, limited closing costs, no PMI) and news.va.gov. Optional nuance: 'no down payment' is not universal (VA says nearly 90% have none) - current summary phrasing is the standard VA marketing description, not flagged. COE: three ways confirmed (online, through lender, by mail with VA Form 26-1880). Eligibility page: must meet credit, income, and occupancy requirements from VA and the lender. Funding fee generally required; exemptions confirmed: receiving VA SC disability compensation, eligible for compensation but receiving retirement/active-duty pay instead, surviving spouses receiving DIC, service members with a pre-discharge proposed/memorandum rating, and active-duty Purple Heart recipients - existing example ('veterans receiving VA disability compensation') accurate. 'Shop with a real estate agent who knows VA appraisals' is advice, not verifiable on official pages. Documents (COE, DD-214, proof of income, bank statements) not contradicted.

Hub: Veteran Readiness and Employment (Chapter 31, formerly Vocational Rehabilitation and Employment) serves service members and Veterans with service-connected disabilities that limit employment; five tracks (reemployment, rapid access to employment, self-employment, long-term services, independent living). Online application lives at https://www.va.gov/careers-employment/vocational-rehabilitation/apply-vre-form-28-1900/. Eligibility confirmed verbatim: no dishonorable discharge; SC disability rating of at least 10%; discharged before 1/1/2013 -> 12-year basic period; on/after 1/1/2013 -> no time limit; serious employment handicap can extend period. How-to-apply: VA Form 28-1900 online, by mail to the VR&E Intake Center (Janesville, WI), in person at a regional office, or with an accredited rep/VSO; then meet a Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor who determines employment handicap, then build a rehabilitation plan - matches existing steps. Optional: whoFor could add 'service members' (hub explicitly includes them) - not an error. Documents (DD-214, rating letter, career goals summary) not contradicted.

categories.notes: VA pension hub: available to some wartime Veterans and their survivors; Aid and Attendance and Housebound are extra pension benefits; Survivors Pension for surviving spouse/child of a deceased wartime Veteran; hotline 800-827-1000. Eligibility page (last updated Sept 3, 2026): no dishonorable discharge; at least 1 day of wartime service with date-dependent active-duty minimums; and at least one of age 65+, permanent and total disability, nursing home care due to disability, or receiving SSDI/SSI; yearly family income and net worth within limits set by Congress (dollar figures on /pension/veterans-pension-rates - not fetched, and VetPath copy does not cite a dollar figure). Existing 'needs-based for wartime veterans who meet age or disability plus income and net-worth limits' is accurate. A&A/Housebound: must already receive VA pension; cannot receive both at once; apply online, by mail (VA Form 21-2680 to Pension Intake Center, Janesville WI), or in person; VA Form 21-0779 if in a nursing home. DFAS: dfas.mil/retiredmilitary/ is bot-blocked (403); dfas.mil WebSearch snippets confirm Retired & Annuitant Pay pays retirees and surviving spouses, SBP pays up to 55% of retired pay and requires an election with premiums, Arrears of Pay beneficiary designation is separate from SBP election, and the SBP-DIC offset was fully eliminated as of the Feb 1, 2023 payday. actionSteps[2] 'Update beneficiaries' is supported by the DFAS AOP guidance. Documents (retirement orders, SBP forms, beneficiary designations) not contradicted.

Hub lists DEA (Chapter 35), Fry Scholarship, GI Bill transfer, CHAMPVA, caregiver support (Caregiver Support Line 855-260-3274), DIC, Survivors Pension, A&A/Housebound, burial, home loans for surviving spouses, FSGLI. DEA: eligible if veteran/service member is P&T disabled from SC disability, died from SC disability, died in line of duty, MIA/captured or forcibly detained >90 days, or hospitalized for SC P&T disability likely leading to discharge; up to 36 months if starting on/after Aug 1, 2018 (45 months before) - existing step accurate. Optional addition: children and spouses who became eligible on/after Aug 1, 2023 have no time limit to use DEA. CHAMPVA: spouse/child of veteran rated P&T disabled from SC disability, or surviving spouse/child of veteran who died from SC disability or was rated P&T at death; must not be eligible for TRICARE; line-of-duty-death exception - existing text accurate (survivor paths not spelled out in sampleEligibility, but 'survivors' are in the whoFor/summary scope; optional enhancement only). PCAFC (page updated Feb 11, 2026): rating 70% or higher (individual or combined), needs at least 6 continuous months of in-person personal care, joint VA Form 10-10CG (online, mail to Janesville WI, or in person) - accurate. caregiver.va.gov support_benefits page is live (updated Sept 14, 2026), names PGCSS as a separate program and describes PCAFC services (stipend, CHAMPVA, counseling, travel, 30+ days respite). GI Bill transfer facts re-confirmed under gi-bill. Documents (marriage/birth certificates, dependent SSNs, DD-214) not contradicted.
